newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA Speyer plant aims for 15 mln dmk in cost-cuts.
newsitem.headline: DASA Speyer plant aims for 15 mln dmk in cost-cuts.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG's plant in Speyer, which is to be taken over by employees, aims to cut costs by 15 million marks in coming years, works council chief Georg Pfeifenroth said on Monday.
DASA announced over the weekend that the plant would become a limited partnership owned by its workforce from January 1, 1997.
The new company, Pfalz KGaA, will have an initial capitalisation of 10 million marks, shares of which will be distributed to workers based on their salaries and length of service.
Pfeifenroth said the savings would be accomplished through a cut in the workforce, longer work hours and reduced payments to the Airbus Industrie consortium.

He said that by adopting a revised work contract, the plant should be able to reduce its workforce to 450 to 500 workers in the next few years from around 570 now and the work week would be extended to 37.5 hours from 35 hours.
He added that the company could save 10 million marks alone by cutting management payments to Airbus.
Pfeifenroth said a contract on the planned savings would be hammered out in the coming weeks.
